code.originalText: Lithium level after the sick visit, prolactin, and the antipsychotic plan

text.paragraph: Lithium level after the sick visit, prolactin, and the antipsychotic plan. [S]

Ms. Fitzgerald returns one week after the sick visit for gastroenteritis, when her lithium level was 1.4 mmol/L. She held lithium for two days as advised, was eating and drinking normally by the third day, and restarted 300 mg twice daily five days ago. The diarrhea stopped within four days. Her tremor is back to a faint shake when she is tired. She admits that she did not go for the lithium level that was due a week after starting, because she felt well and forgot. Her mood is better, and she has had no manic or psychotic symptoms. She saw the sports dietitian and is eating three meals and two snacks; she has started one gentle class a day. Her periods have not returned. She has had no thoughts of suicide or self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1930-06-08; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well and well hydrated; weight 50.2 kg; blood pressure 104/66, pulse 74
Very faint fine postural tremor; no ataxia; no akathisia or rigidity
Brighter; organized; no psychotic or manic features

First episode of psychosis with marked mood symptoms: about three weeks of little sleep, rapid speech, racing thoughts, grandiose plans and very long training days, then a voice commenting on her dancing and a belief that she was being watched and tested; tearful low mood since discharge. Diagnosis provisional; differential: bipolar I disorder with psychotic features, schizoaffective disorder (bipolar type), and schizophreniform disorder or schizophrenia, depending on whether the psychosis ever occurred apart from the mood symptoms. Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented first hospitalization

S — Synthetic modern coding of the documented first breakdown. Unspecified psychosis is coded until the course shows how the psychosis relates to the mood symptoms; superseded at the three-month visit.
Secondary amenorrhea: no periods for about four months before admission, during very heavy dance training at a low weight (BMI 18.7), with prolactin raised on risperidone; pregnancy test negative
S — Synthetic presenting finding linked to her documented training; resolved when her periods returned.
Acute viral gastroenteritis (vomiting and watery diarrhea for two days, roommate with the same illness), with mild dehydration; resolved
S — Synthetic acute infection; not a historical claim.
Lithium level above the therapeutic range (1.4 mmol/L) during dehydration, with nausea and a worse fine tremor, without confusion or unsteadiness; lithium held and restarted; resolved
S — Synthetic medication adverse effect at a prescribed dose; ICD-10-CM classifies lithium salts with the other antipsychotics and neuroleptics.

Secondary amenorrhea (N91.1). Prolactin still raised at 66 ng/mL, and no period. Energy intake has improved with the dietitian's plan, so risperidone is now the factor that can be changed. Aripiprazole spares prolactin and has a lower metabolic risk. [S]

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Canadian Network for Mood and Anxiety Treatments (CANMAT) and International Society for Bipolar Disorders (ISBD) 2018 guidelines for the management of patients with bipolar disorder (2018); The CANMAT and ISBD Guidelines for the Treatment of Bipolar Disorder: Summary and a 2023 Update of Evidence (2023); The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Schizophrenia, Third Edition (2020); Consensus development conference on antipsychotic drugs and obesity and diabetes (2004); Recovery After an Initial Schizophrenia Episode (RAISE): coordinated specialty care for first-episode psychosis (2026); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, depression, bipolar, and mood disorders monograph (2026)

Follow-up: Three-month visit in nine weeks, fasting, with lithium level, kidney and thyroid tests, calcium, prolactin, glucose, A1c, and lipids. Care coordinator weekly. Next scheduled visit 1930-08-10: three-month review: lithium, thyroid, kidney and metabolic checks, and the diagnosis reviewed. [S]
